Attendance and Leave Management Narrative QA Report

A storytelling walkthrough of the Attendance and Leave QA exercise, linking HR use cases, demo data, product navigation, expected behavior, actual evidence, and production hardening.

Total Checks30
Passed30
Needs Fix0

How To Read This Document

  • Each scenario is written as a realistic HR workflow, not just a technical check.
  • Navigation steps show how a user reaches the feature in AuroraHR.
  • Expected and actual outcomes make the product behavior auditable.
  • Screenshots are embedded as proof for investor, customer, and internal QA review.
  • Important boundary: this is now post-deploy strict evidence. Earlier baseline gaps remain documented separately in the QA evidence audit.

Executive Narrative

This document follows the daily employee and HR operating rhythm: employees record attendance and apply for leave, managers approve exceptions, HR intervenes where required, and leadership reviews company-level health. The post-deploy strict QA pass verified the core workflows, backend persistence paths, reporting APIs, and role-specific visual surfaces.

Attendance / Employee

Daily attendance self-service and monthly attendance history

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

Employees need a simple daily check-in/check-out experience and a transparent monthly record of their attendance, late marks, work hours, and exceptions.

Sample Data and Persona

Persona: Neha Shah, demo employee. Date range: May 2026. The run also exercised clock-in and clock-out guard behavior so repeat submissions do not corrupt attendance.

Product Navigation

  1. Log in as demo.employee@aurorahr.in.
  2. Open Attendance from the left navigation.
  3. Review the Today attendance card, monthly selector, status cards, and attendance table.
  4. Use Export when a monthly attendance file is required.

Expected Outcome

The employee should see only their own attendance, current day status, monthly records, and available self-service actions.

Actual Outcome

The employee view rendered correctly and the backend clock endpoints behaved safely for repeated execution.

Attendance / Employee and Manager

Attendance regularization request and approval

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

When an employee forgets to punch in/out or works from an alternate location, they should request regularization. The manager or HR should approve or reject with an auditable outcome.

Sample Data and Persona

Two regularization requests were created for the demo employee. One was approved by the manager and one was rejected by HR.

Product Navigation

  1. Employee opens Attendance.
  2. Employee opens Request Regularization.
  3. Employee enters date, requested check-in/check-out, and reason.
  4. Manager opens Attendance > Requests.
  5. Manager approves; HR can intervene and reject other pending requests.

Expected Outcome

Pending regularizations should appear in the approver queue and approval should update the attendance record.

Actual Outcome

Regularization creation, manager approval, and HR rejection all passed.

Leave / Employee

Employee leave balance review and leave application

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

Employees need to understand leave balances before applying and then submit a leave request with dates, type, and reason.

Sample Data and Persona

Persona: Neha Shah. The visual run shows casual, sick, and earned leave balances plus pending, approved, and rejected requests.

Product Navigation

  1. Log in as employee.
  2. Open Leave Management.
  3. Review balance cards and request history.
  4. Click Apply Leave to open the application modal.

Expected Outcome

The employee should see available leave balances and create a request without seeing team or HR-only data.

Actual Outcome

Leave balances, request history, and apply leave modal rendered correctly.

Leave / Manager and HR

Manager approval and HR intervention

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

Managers approve routine leave requests for their team. HR should be able to intervene for exceptions, policy control, or rejected cases.

Sample Data and Persona

One employee casual leave was approved by the manager. One sick leave request was rejected by HR to verify intervention controls.

Product Navigation

  1. Manager opens Leave Management > Team Approvals.
  2. Manager reviews pending request and approves.
  3. HR opens Leave Management > Team Approvals/all requests.
  4. HR rejects another pending request with comments.

Expected Outcome

Approvers should see only actionable team/company requests based on role and record decisions with comments.

Actual Outcome

Manager approval and HR rejection both passed and were visible in the role-specific UI.

Attendance / HR

Company attendance control, mass update, and sync

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

HR needs a daily company view for exceptions, and operational tools to correct attendance in bulk or import device/file attendance data.

Sample Data and Persona

The run verified HR company attendance and backend bulk update. Later hardening wired mass update and CSV sync to real persistence and removed mock device data.

Product Navigation

  1. Log in as HR.
  2. Open Attendance > Company.
  3. Review daily company attendance cards and table.
  4. Open Mass Update for bulk corrections.
  5. Open Sync for device/file import.

Expected Outcome

HR should see company-wide controls and any correction/import should persist through backend APIs with audit fields.

Actual Outcome

Post-deploy strict QA verified the backend bulk update path and asserted both the Mass Attendance Update and Sync Attendance modals render. CSV-backed sync now saves valid rows through the backend bulk-update path.

Reports / HR and Leadership

Attendance and leave reporting

Passed

HR Process Being Tested

HR and leadership need date-range reporting to understand attendance health, leave usage, department-level patterns, and exceptions.

Sample Data and Persona

The test queried attendance statistics, department attendance, and leave statistics for the demo tenant.

Product Navigation

  1. HR opens Attendance.
  2. HR selects Reports after the production hardening update.
  3. HR chooses date range and reviews summary cards, department breakdown, leave summary, and CSV export.

Expected Outcome

Reporting APIs and UI should return accurate department and leave metrics without query failures.

Actual Outcome

Post-deploy strict QA verified attendance statistics, department attendance statistics, leave statistics, leadership views, and the HR Reports tab without query failures.
